purpose: Cross-world inventory and asset identity for special-rendered cloud type 0x28.

runtime.resource_selector_note: WOLKE.BOB is not independently requested by the normal per-level resource batch; the callback uses a special renderer with object+0x12=FFFF.

player_state_probe.controls: camera=(700,100); synthetic DS:881A points at cloud object; DS:89EA=0; bounds fields +0x2C/+0x30=0/16 and +0x2E/+0x32=0/16; object+0x37=0
player_state_probe.conclusion: The native 9269 branch writes DS:89E6=FFFF only when the persistent bounds gate is active and player object byte +0x37 is zero; the controlled positive probe keeps the cloud stationary and callback active.

player_reader_probe.controls: same W1L1 synthetic cloud state; one-shot breakpoint after the 9269 callback
player_reader_probe.conclusion: Both player-side DS:89E6 readers execute in the positive synthetic state, so the cloud flag is consumed by the player callback path rather than being write-only.

renderer_static_scan.standard_renderer: 01F7:3529 returns immediately when object+0x12 == 0xFFFF, so the cloud does not use the normal DS:6D8E logical-slot path.
renderer_static_scan.outer_state_consumer: The main gameplay loop at 01D7:4EA0 tests DS:89E6; the positive path begins at 01D7:4EAA and runs through the outer/main-loop work before the normal object-render pass at 01F7:106A. A controlled trace hits 01D7:4EA0 repeatedly with DS:89E6=FFFF while the cloud object remains active.

hardware_renderer_probe.controls: W1 synthetic type-0x28 cloud, forced player-state gate, camera=(768,192), 64 frame samples
hardware_renderer_probe.interpretation: The bounded hardware hook saw only an ordinary logical-slot draw (slot 276), not WOLKE slots 413-416. This is negative evidence against the special cloud draw being emitted by the normal per-frame queue in this fixture; it does not identify the low-level WOLKE caller.

wolke_descriptor_map_probe.controls: Isolated W1L1 type-0x28 variant at camera=(700,100), forced cloud player-state gate, 8 samples at 01F7:0013; snapshot DS:6D8A/DS:6D8E descriptor map for logical slots 413-416 before the draw loop.
wolke_descriptor_map_probe.interpretation: The four WOLKE logical slots are unmapped in the ordinary DS:6D8E descriptor table in this live fixture, while the same hook continues to see a normal mapped draw. This strengthens the conclusion that WOLKE is rendered through a special/alternate path rather than a normal queue entry; it does not yet identify the alternate pixel primitive or frame-selection state.

direct_caller_census.interpretation: The normal queue caller is unique among the recovered direct forms. Any WOLKE-specific draw must be indirect, use another primitive, or be reached through runtime state not represented by a direct call to 0013.

renderer_static_scan.conclusion: The cloud callback contains no direct sprite/resource call. The normal object renderer is still explicitly bypassed (01F7:3529 sees the cloud object at ES:DI and object+0x12=FFFF), while the outer gameplay loop consumes DS:89E6 at 01D7:4EA0. The four WOLKE slots also remain unmapped in DS:6D8E during a live special-state fixture, closing another ordinary-queue boundary. The exact WOLKE.BOB pixel-draw primitive remains outside the normal logical-slot queue.

conclusion: Type 0x28 is used in every world, but the cloud asset is one global WOLKE.BOB table rather than WOLKE_Wn.BOB variants. The player-state gate and the outer DS:89E6 consumer are directly evidenced; the normal logical-slot renderer is bypassed, leaving only the low-level WOLKE.BOB pixel-draw primitive to identify.
